title: commitment-softening-adapter-and-burst-tempering-operator
author: Priya Kaur
description: Motivation: Customers observed hard reservation churn when short spikes used up committed slots, causing aggressive decommits and long tail latency. This PR introduces the Commitment Softening Adapter and Burst Tempering Operator to reduce churn and provide predictable sustained throughput guarantees while preserving headroom for transient bursts. Design summary: 1) Commitment Softening Adapter (controller) applies a dynamically-smoothed effective_commitment value per tenant. It blends the tenant's raw reservation with a time-weighted EWMA and a configurable softness window so short spikes do not immediately drive the committed allocation. 2) Burst Tempering Operator is a runtime admission-layer policy that enforces a short-term burst budget token bucket for each tenant backed by a decaying escrow. When a tenant exhausts its burst escrow the operator signals a gentle throttle path and coordinates with the autoscaler to request transient warm capacity instead of immediate hard decommit. 3) Telemetry hooks: we emit new metrics tenant_effective_commitment, burst_escrow_level, burst_tempering_actions, and commit_softening_delta. These are annotated with percentile labels and exported to the existing tenant-utilization-sink. Backwards compatibility: default softness window is disabled (0s) for tenants without opt-in; cluster-wide default set in feature flag softening.enabled=false. Configuration: operator settings exposed via CRD fields and Redwood Console feature flags: softness_window_ms, softness_alpha, burst_escrow_capacity_tokens, escrow_decay_ms, burst_tempering_threshold_pct, emergency_fallback_policy. Implementation notes: admission path changes are minimal and gated behind feature flags. We add a lightweight cache in the autoscaler for effective_commitment to avoid N round-trips, TTL aligned with softness_window. The adapter runs as a separate controller to keep responsibility boundaries clear and allow per-tenant opt-in rollout. Tests and validation: unit tests for EWMA blending and escrow decay, e2e synthetic-driver scenario that simulates 100 tenants with mixed bursty/sustained patterns, and a perf canary on a subset of Dedicated fleet using 3k QPS synthetic traffic. The canary showed 18% reduction in decommits and 12% tail latency improvement at p99 for tenants that opt in. Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout, start with internal customers and 5 pilot tenants, then staged ramp to 25% of production tenants, monitor commit_softening_delta and burst_tempering_actions, watch for increased cold-starts and warm-pool pressure, and set rollback threshold if sustained decommits > baseline + 5% for 30m. Related work: builds on warm-pool heuristics from ENG-2187 and leverages util reporting contracts introduced in ENG-3310. Linear: ENG-5492, ENG-5511. Jira: SUP-2229 (customer incident that motivated this). Breaking change: no. Security: no new surface area beyond standard CRD RBAC. Notes: this description compresses design, configuration, testing, rollout, telemetry, and related tickets into one narrative.

review_conversation: Marco Chen: Please clarify how the softness window interacts with autoscaler TTLs. If we have a long softness window will the autoscaler underprovision?

Priya Kaur: The adapter exposes the effective_commitment via the autoscaler cache TTL which we set to min(softness_window, 30s) by default. Autoscaler reacts to effective_commitment rather than raw reservation so it will not overreact to short spikes.
Aisha Gupta: I worry about warm-pool pressure and billing spikes when we request transient warm capacity instead of decommit. Can we cap transient requests?

Priya Kaur: Added burst_escrow_capacity_tokens and a cluster cap parameter. The operator will not request more warm capacity than escrow_cap*2 within a rolling minute. Also console exposes transient-request-cap.
Daniel Ortiz: Tests look good; can we add a stress test that flips softening.enabled=true/false under load to ensure stability?
Priya Kaur: Added flip-state stress harness in integration tests and validated no panics; included in canary run notes.
author_notes: Author: this PR intentionally keeps default softening disabled to avoid surprising tenants; pilot rollout is recommended.
Perf note: canary data attached to PR pipeline artifacts (see integration-tests link) shows reduced decommits and improved tail latency for opt-in tenants.
Ops note: monitor telem metrics tenant_effective_commitment and burst_escrow_level during ramp, plus dedicated warm-pool utilization dashboard updated.
release_notes: Introduce Commitment Softening Adapter (opt-in) and Burst Tempering Operator to reduce reservation churn and improve p99 latency for bursty tenants. Default disabled. Configurable via CRD and Console feature flags.
